item.content:encoded: Daphne police are searching for a suspect after a bank robbery at Merchants Marine Bank just before 1 p.m. Friday, according to Daphne Police Chief Brian Gulsby. item.title: Car crashes through Mobile storefront, damages two shops
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees

The incident occurred when a car drove through the storefront of one of the shops. Both a Cato and Hibbett Sports location sustained damage from the crash. Mobile police…
item.content:encoded:
A vehicle crashed through the front of a retail store in Mobile Thursday afternoon, causing damage to multiple businesses in the area, according to Mobile Police Department.

The incident occurred when a car drove through the storefront of one of the shops. Both a Cato and Hibbett Sports location sustained damage from the crash.

Mobile police responded to the scene and are investigating the circumstances surrounding the collision. Details about injuries, the cause of the crash, and the extent of damage to both stores were not immediately available.

The investigation remains ongoing as authorities work to determine how the vehicle ended up crashing through the storefront.

item.title: Niceville Fire Engine, Chief Head to Texas for Wildfire Relief
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The Niceville Fire Department has sent one engine and a Battalion Chief to Texas to assist in battling large-scale wildfires, according to department officials. The deployment is part of regional mutual aid efforts to support firefighting operations in Texas. Officials emphasized that the move will not affect service levels for Niceville…
item.content:encoded:
The Niceville Fire Department has sent one engine and a Battalion Chief to Texas to assist in battling large-scale wildfires, according to department officials.

The deployment is part of regional mutual aid efforts to support firefighting operations in Texas. Officials emphasized that the move will not affect service levels for Niceville residents, as the department maintains adequate resources to handle local emergency response.

This type of cross-state assistance is common during major fire seasons, allowing departments across the country to share personnel and equipment to combat large wildfires that can quickly overwhelm local resources.

item.title: Pensacola's Graffiti Bridge honors Dolly Parton with new mural

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola's iconic Graffiti Bridge has been transformed into a tribute to country music legend Dolly Parton following her recent death. The mural joins countless other memorials being created around the world as fans and artists grapple with the loss of the legendary performer, according to WKRG News 5.

The Graffiti Bridge, a beloved local landmark known for its ever-changing street art, has become a gathering place for community expression and remembrance. The Dolly Parton mural represents one of the latest additions to the bridge's ongoing artistic canvas, where residents and visitors have long left their marks.

Parton's influence on music and popular culture spanned decades, and her passing prompted an outpouring of tributes from fans worldwide. Pensacola's artistic community chose to honor her legacy through one of the city's most recognizable public art spaces, ensuring that her memory will be visible to thousands who cross the bridge daily.

item.title: Fort Walton Beach Lowe's hosts bed-building event for local children
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees

item.content:encoded:
Volunteers are being sought to help construct beds for children in need during a community service event at the Fort Walton Beach Lowe's, according to organizers.

The effort brings together Lowe's, the nonprofit Sleep in Heavenly Peace, and local volunteers to build and donate beds to children in the Fort Walton Beach area who might otherwise go without. Sleep in Heavenly Peace operates across the country with a mission focused on ensuring every child has a safe place to sleep.

The event offers residents a chance to get hands-on with a meaningful project while supporting families facing housing insecurity or financial hardship. No carpentry experience is necessary, and all materials and tools are typically provided by the organizing partners.

Interested volunteers can contact Lowe's or reach out to Sleep in Heavenly Peace for event details and sign-up information.

item.title: Mobile County Schools Earn National Recognition for Attendance Gains
item.dc:creator: Robert Rees
item.description: The Mobile County Public School System is being recognized nationally for making significant strides in reducing chronic absenteeism, according to a school system news release. Attendance Works, an organization that tracks school attendance patterns across the country, credited MCPSS with "impressive progress" in addressing what has become a…
item.content:encoded:
The Mobile County Public School System is being recognized nationally for making significant strides in reducing chronic absenteeism, according to a school system news release. Attendance Works, an organization that tracks school attendance patterns across the country, credited MCPSS with "impressive progress" in addressing what has become a widespread challenge in American education.

Chronic absenteeism—typically defined as missing 10 percent or more of school days—has been identified by education experts as a critical factor affecting student achievement and long-term outcomes. The recognition suggests Mobile County's efforts to keep students in classrooms are paying off.

The school system did not immediately provide specific attendance figures or detail which programs or initiatives drove the improvement. MCPSS serves more than 60,000 students across Mobile County.

item.content:encoded:
A waterspout formed off the coast of Dauphin Island Friday morning, according to WKRG News 5. Photos captured the phenomenon near the Sand Island Lighthouse, where the rotating column of air and water was visible to observers in the area.

Waterspouts are relatively common along the Alabama and Northwest Florida coasts during certain weather conditions, particularly when warm water meets unstable atmospheric conditions. While they can occasionally pose a threat to watercraft, most waterspouts dissipate quickly as they move onshore.

The National Weather Service monitors these developments as part of regular coastal weather surveillance. Boaters in the area are typically advised to exercise caution when waterspout activity is reported.

item.title: Chilling texts revealed as Isabelle Johnson faces detention hearing in Walton County

According to WKRG News 5, the hearing revealed disturbing text messages that prosecutors say demonstrate the severity of the case against her. Johnson had been a fugitive for nearly…
item.content:encoded:
Isabelle Johnson appeared in a Walton County courtroom Wednesday for a pretrial detention hearing as prosecutors seek to determine whether she'll be released on bond. According to WKRG News 5, the hearing revealed disturbing text messages that prosecutors say demonstrate the severity of the case against her.

Johnson had been a fugitive for nearly two months before investigators located her at a residence in Cottondale. The details of those texts—and what they allegedly show about her mindset—appear central to the state's argument for keeping her in custody without bond.

The case has drawn significant attention in the region, with Johnson's extended time on the run raising questions about circumstances surrounding her arrest. Prosecutors characterized the messages as evidence of her state of mind, though specifics of the texts and the underlying charges have not been fully disclosed publicly.

The outcome of Wednesday's hearing will determine whether Johnson faces the remainder of her proceedings from jail or is released pending trial.

item.content:encoded:
A Mobile County man has been sentenced to five years in federal prison on a fentanyl trafficking conviction, according to a Department of Justice announcement. Horatio Tremaine Washington received the 60-month sentence, part of ongoing federal efforts to combat the distribution of fentanyl across the region.

The case adds to a growing number of trafficking prosecutions in the Mobile and surrounding areas as law enforcement agencies work to disrupt the flow of the synthetic opioid, which has become a major contributor to overdose deaths nationwide. Federal authorities have made fentanyl trafficking a priority given the drug's potency and the danger it poses to communities.

item.content:encoded: A Walton County judge has ordered Isabelle Johnson held without bond after she was captured following a nearly two-month manhunt. Johnson is now facing first-degree premeditated murder charges in connection with the death of Jason Coulthart, according to reporting from WKRG News 5. The judge's decision came after taking nearly 24 hours to consider the bond request. Johnson had been wanted on an open murder charge before authorities apprehended her and upgraded the charges to first-degree premeditated murder. She remains in custody pending trial.

Forecasters warn, however, that it could still produce heavy rain in parts of the Caribbean. The Leeward…
item.content:encoded: Tropical Storm Dolly is expected to bring heavy rain to the Caribbean Islands this weekend. The storm currently has sustained winds of 40 miles per hour as it races across the Atlantic, and is expected to weaken as it reaches the islands. Forecasters warn, however, that it could still produce heavy rain in parts of the Caribbean. The Leeward Islands could see heavy rain on Saturday, with Puerto Rico and the Virgin Islands getting hit on Sunday and Monday. Island residents are being told to prepare for gusty winds and flash flooding.

item.title: DeSantis Slams Grand Jury Report
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis is pushing back hard against a grand jury report that says ten-million dollars from a Medicaid settlement was improperly steered through the Hope Florida Foundation for political purposes. Speaking Thursday in Lake City, DeSantis called the report's findings false, insisting the money was a legal, private contribution — not…
item.content:encoded: Governor Ron DeSantis is pushing back hard against a grand jury report that says ten-million dollars from a Medicaid settlement was improperly steered through the Hope Florida Foundation for political purposes. Speaking Thursday in Lake City, DeSantis called the report's findings false, insisting the money was a legal, private contribution — not diverted Medicaid funds. He labeled the entire investigation a politically motivated "hoax" targeting his administration and First Lady Casey DeSantis.The governor stressed the grand jury found no probable cause for criminal charges. The report claims the money helped fund opposition to a marijuana legalization amendment.
